statements.anchor:
Students should not use ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Gemini, Claude, or
any other generative AI chatbot
statements.label: no AI tools on homework
statements.passage:
Students should not use ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Gemini, Claude, or
any other generative AI chatbot, AI tool within an integrated
development environment (IDE), or AI software development assistant
while working on their homework assignments for this course. While
these tools can instantaneously produce plausible solutions for some
typical or introductory programming exercises, relianace on these
tools for introductory program is a crutch and students will lose the
opportunity to learn the fundamentals we aim to teach in this course
through homework assignments. Some students wrongly assume that
carefully reading through the solution created by an AI, tutor, or
peer is sufficient to learn the concepts covered in the assignment.
Note that exams in this course will be paper and pencil without access
to the internet or AI tools. Students who have over-relied on tutors
or AI tools for homework will not be prepared to solve new problems
and to succeed on these exams. Furthermore, the hiring process for
software internships and full-time positions is changing in response
to applicants who attempt to use ChatGPT or similar tools during
interviews. Statements such as "The use of generative AI during the
interview is not permitted" and "Applicant must not be reliant on
ChatGPT to communicate effectively with business representatives" now
commonly appear on job postings.

statements.anchor: Treat information from online searches and generative AI (such as ChatGPT) the same way as discussions with your classmates.
statements.label: AI treated like classmate discussion
statements.passage:
Treat information from online searches and generative AI (such as ChatGPT) the same way as discussions with your classmates. In particular, you are not allowed to copy answers or (parts of) code from other sources - your submission needs to be created entirely on your own/with your partner. If a resource happens to include a solution to the problem, do not read it in full: use it as a resource for hints.

Discussions with other human beings is strongly preferred to other sources.

Information obtained via a discussion, online search, or generative AI has to be attributed:
At the end of each relevant submission, include a section headed "Resources" where you describe the nature of the conversation with your classmates (a paragraph or so), or the specific online/genAI prompts you used and the obtained results (urls and/or screenshots of the engine's responses).

statements.anchor: ChatGPT and other Generative AI tools are not considered to be part of the official toolkit.
statements.label: AI not in official toolkit
statements.passage:
ChatGPT/ AI Policy

Need to know

CAUTIONARY:
ChatGPT and other Generative AI tools are not considered to be part of the official toolkit. It is important that you understand that the skills and knowledge you will gain in this course constitute the
fundamentals
and we want to make sure you have a
solid understanding
. The knowledge and skills required for your career, which you will exercise here, are not ones that can be gained by prompting for an automated response. We ask that you explore but also approach with skepticism and apply your own critical thinking in pursuing actual sources and in augmenting what you learn in class. From time to time you may be asked to use these tools.

That said, we want to hear from you if/how you are using, and/or benefitting from using, these technologies. Remember that tools are only part of, and not the basis, of your learning. For specific details on policy of what is acceptable for this course be sure to review the following sections.

Original Student work

All student work is required to be their own. While we encourage research and reuse, all submissions must be your own, original creation. Copying/ Plagiarism/ Examination assistance are NOT tolerated. This is standard policy. This applies to ALL work, be it code related or written/ essay style submission.

Use of a GPT/ AI

Again, all work is required to be your original creation. In other words, anything you submit must not have been created or modified by any AI means. Unless given instruction for a specific allowed use, the only place where you may use GPT or other AI tools is for searching and/or reference, the following provisons apply:

Submit your prompts for GPT (as a separate file) as part of your work

Provide a confirming statement that GPT was used as reference only, and your work is original

code from another student, submitting AI-generated code or text, or copying from other sources is
considered plagiarism.

to do so may result in a penalty, including a reduction in grade.

University Course Description

An overview of software engineering techniques for producing high-quality software systems. Students will participate in a software development team.

Course Prerequisites

Completion of
COP 4530 (Data Structures)
with a minimum grade of C-.

Course Topics

Software and Software Engineering

Software Activities and Tasks

Software Process Philosophies, Models, and Methodologies

Software Requirements Analysis

Software Project Management

Software Quality

Software Design

Software Construction

Software Testing

Software Maintenance

Student Learning Outcomes

At the end of the course, you will be able to:

Discuss system development life cycle (SDLC)

Critique different software process models

Select and tailor software methodology for a software project

Elicit and analyze requirements for a software product to write and evaluate

Completion of
COP 4530 (Data Structures)

Software Activities and Tasks

Software Process Philosophies, Models, and Methodologies

Software Requirements Analysis

Software Project Management

Software Quality

Software Design

Software Construction

Software Testing

Software Maintenance

Discuss system development life cycle (SDLC)

Critique different software process models

Select and tailor software methodology for a software project

Elicit and analyze requirements for a software product to write and evaluate

statements.label: asked to avoid AI on homework
statements.passage:
Collaboration, Academic Integrity, and Policy for AI-generated work: Coding, like exercise or weight
training, cannot produce their intended benefit when others do what you should do for yourself. Thus,
we OFFICIALLY ask that you do the assignments yourself without the help of others or AI -assistance.
Only by struggling through the homework (programming) tasks, will you prepare yourself for the exams
and future courses.

However, we realize that computational thinking is difficult and debugging code can sometimes by
arduous. While you will grow the most by doing that on your own and asking for help from course staff
(TAs, tutors, and the instructor), we will allow you to submit code that you have developed through
collaboration with other students or through the help of AI assistance. If you DO use these resources we
ask that you:
A.) Cite the source in the code itself (i.e. as a comment around the code you received help on, list ing
the name of individual(s) who you worked with or the AI-assistance tool you used), AND

Page 3

B.) When you submit your code, check the boxes indicating the sources you used just above the "Mark
as Complete" button. There is NO SHAME OR PENALTY for checking these boxes. We want to
accurately know (and potentially develop better help alternatives or gain valuable insight for future
engineering education endeavors) what assignments are difficult and what fraction of our
population is served by collaboration or AI. (We may also be able to afford you additional help from
course staff so that you do not HAVE TO rely on external tools or assistance), AND
C.) REALIZE that using these forms of assistance very likely means you may NOT be prepared for the
exams, where you will NOT be allowed to collaborate or use AI assistance. We let you use these
resources on homeworks so that hopefully you can learn workable approaches and more easily
overcome blocks in future assignments. Again, we prefer you just get help from course staff. But
too much reliance on other sources of input means your readiness for the exams and future courses
may be low.

Notes for Future Courses. CS courses produce a considerable number (likely a majority) of academic
integrity cases at the university. This is because what constitutes collaboration or use of online
resources can sometimes be a gray area. Our policy this semester is more liberal in an effort to avoid
some of these issues. But future CS courses will likely have STRICT collaboration and AI-Assistance

statements.anchor: we do not allow AI use for any reason in this course.
statements.label: AI banned for any reason
statements.passage:
Collaboration, Academic Integrity, and Policy for AI-generated work: Coding, like exercise or weight
training, cannot produce its intended benefit when others do what you should do for yourself. Thus, we
do not allow AI use for any reason in this course. Only by struggling through the homework and
projects, will you prepare yourself for the exams and future courses. With that said, please follow the
rules below to avoid Academic Integrity Violations.

Collaboration/AI Policy for Homework Assignments: May be done individually or in teams of 2. You
must list your team member in your source code as a comment on the top line. The intent of
homework is to develop your basic skill set and understanding of lecture material. Because use of
generative AI would remove any of that benefit, we do not allow its use.

Collaboration/AI Policy for Projects and Exams: Projects and exams must be completed individually
(except for the team-based lab project later in the semester) and MAY NOT use AI, help from other
students / 3rd parties, or external solutions even for reference. You are NEVER allowed to show,
verbally describe, or otherwise share any part of your code with another student. You should NOT
verbally describe your code or guide another student on what to write or what to do. Furthermore,
coding together on projects should be done with caution. Developing similar pseudocode or even
planning together when done at a detailed level can lead to code that is essentially the same (and really
a team effort vs. an individual effort) and is considered a violation. Finally, copying (and then
modification) or just “viewing for reference” any portion of code from Internet sources (including AI or
websites) or fellow students is prohibited.

COLLABORATION OR AI USAGE OUTSIDE OF THESE GUIDELINES WILL LEAD TO ACADEMIC INTEGRITY
VIOLATIONS AND WILL BE REPORTED TO THE OFFICE OF ACADEMIC INTEGRITY

Here are two examples to demonstrate what you can and cannot ask an AI:

I need to write a findPerfects() function that returns whether a number is a perfect number or not.

I don’t understand how when I would use a set over a vector in C++. Can you give me some reasons when
one is better than the other?

statements.label: develop own coding skills
statements.passage:
Use of Generative AI Tools

While artificial intelligence (AI) tools can be valuable in certain contexts, in this course it is important that you develop your own skills and abilities to write, debug and think critically. For the assignments in this course, it will be the effort and process (not just the product) that is most valuable to your learning, and while useful, AI tools can inhibit the gains from working through this process when used improperly.

For that reason,
you should only use AI tools in the same way that you would ask a friend in the class for help, as documented above
– high level questions, citations where needed, etc. For example, you should not use AI tools to write code/responses for you on assignments or any graded work. Doing so is a violation of the Stanford Honor Code. Instead, please take advantage of the support resources above - we are eager to help!

you submit, nor does it change the expectations of academic integrity described below.
